messages:
customer-alex: Hey team — started seeing a bunch of 400s from the embeddings endpoint this morning. Our batch job (50 items) returns: 

Error: 400 Bad Request - embedding vector length mismatch (expected 1536, got 0)

Only ~10 items fail but they trigger retries and a billing spike. We suspect some inputs are empty or non-strings after our dedupe step.

Here's an example of a failing request body (redacted):
```json
{
  \"model\": \"open-embed-1536\",
  \"input\": [\"good text\", [], \"another\", null, \"\", \"more\"]
}
```

Also possible we double-stringify somewhere (we use JSON.stringify on a list in some code paths). Any ideas?

maya-s: Thanks — can you paste the raw POST (headers + body) for one failing call? Also what's the client lib + version? Creating SUP-4721. :eyes:

support-bot: Ticket SUP-4721 created and linked to thread.

customer-alex: Raw headers: 
```
Authorization: Bearer ***
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
```
Raw body (failing example):
```json
{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":"[\"good text\", \"another\"]"}
```
So in some flows we end up sending the array as a string (JSON.stringify applied twice). Also sometimes an empty array element shows up because our dedupe returns [] for missing content.

jordan-ops: Ah — two distinct problems: 1) double-stringified array (server receives a single string, tries to parse as text -> yields wrong shape) and 2) nested/empty items inside the input array ([], null, \"\"). Both can lead to zero-length vectors or parser errors.

kevin-eng: Confirming: server expects either a single string (scalar) or an array of strings. If we get a string that looks like JSON (e.g. \"[\\\"a\\\",\\\"b\\\"]\"), our handler currently treats it as a scalar string and will attempt to encode it which results in unexpected tokenization/embedding size. Nested arrays/empty values cause the batching kernel to compute a 0-length vector for that item which shows as length mismatch.

kevin-eng: Quick repro (curl):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":"[\"hello\",\""]"}'
```
This will appear to succeed but downstream will throw shape errors when the runtime expects 1536 floats but gets 0 for some entries.

maya-s: For a short-term mitigation, normalize on the client: ensure `input` is always an array of non-empty strings. Example JS helper to add to the shipper (one-liner):
```js
const normalizeInputs = arr => (Array.isArray(arr) ? arr.flat().filter(x => x !== null && x !== undefined && String(x).trim() !== \"\").map(String) : [String(arr)]);
```
Call `normalizeInputs(payload.input)` before sending. Also make sure you don't JSON.stringify the array when posting with `Content-Type: application/json` (axios/fetch will do it for you).

customer-alex: That helps, thanks — we'll patch the dedupe step to return nulls filtered out and remove the extra stringify. Quick question: are we being billed for the bad rows? We saw an unexpected billing bump from yesterday.

jordan-ops: Short answer: yes, currently the hosting billing counts tokens at request time even if downstream fails later. We're logging this as a billing impact in SUP-4721. Ops will review refunds for clearly malformed batches.

kevin-eng: Longer term: I'll add stricter server-side validation in the next sprint so malformed elements return a clear 400 with index-level error text like: \"400: input[3] invalid: nested array/null/empty string\" and avoid charging for malformed items. I'll put this as a low-risk fix and aim for the end of sprint (2 weeks).

maya-s: For now, can you attach one failing request ID (response headers should include `x-request-id`) and the time of the call so we can correlate logs? That will let ops scope the billing impact.

customer-alex: Got it — one example x-request-id: rwd-9f3c7a and timestamp 2026-03-16T14:22:11Z. We'll push the client fix tonight.

jordan-ops: Great. I'll hold SUP-4721 open until engineering ships the validation. If you want us to process a refund for that window, confirm the list of affected request-ids in the ticket.

customer-alex: Thanks all — immediate workaround applied (normalizeInputs) and retesting. Will post results here. :thumbsup:

kevin-eng: Thanks — also adding a short note to the docs: \"Embeddings input must be either a single string or an array of strings; nested arrays, nulls, and empty strings will produce errors.\"

customer-alex: Verified — no more 400s after the fix. Closing out once ops confirms billing.
